Submitted. Everything below is **model prediction, not measurement** — no assay was run and no fitness outcome is claimed.

## What I could and couldn't measure

Two evidence gaps shaped this ranking, and they matter more than the ranking itself:

- **No evolutionary channel.** `blast_msa`, `blast_search`, and `mmseqs_search` all require an existing workspace reference FASTA; none is present (I probed two paths). So `pssm_score` and `conservation` could not be run at all.
- **No burial measurement.** `mkdssp` rejects the ESMFold artifact (`did not start with a valid PDB HEADER line`). Every buried-vs-exposed claim below is *inferred* from ESM-IF1 penalties, not measured.

That leaves ESM-2 masked marginals and ESM-IF1 on the ESMFold backbone — both ESM-family, so correlated rather than independent. I scored all 100 candidates on ESM-2, then cross-checked the top tier on ESM-IF1.

Calibration was good: WT gave `native_sequence_match: true` (mean LL −1.31343), confirming the backbone encodes WT — which also means ESM-IF1 is biased *against* all mutants, so positive deltas are the real signal. Controls behaved: I23E (−11.81 / −16.6 nats) and Y61E (−9.95 / −12.6) were both crushed.

## The ten, ranked

| # | Variant | ESM-2 Δ | ESM-IF Δ (nats) | BLOSUM |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **D33E** | +0.46 | **+1.85** | +2 |
| 2 | **R51K** | **+1.91** | +0.33 | +2 |
| 3 | G21S | +1.21 | −0.76 | 0 |
| 4 | E66D | −0.13 | +0.57 | +2 |
| 5 | R53K | −1.18 | +1.55 | +2 |
| 6 | A25Q | −0.82 | +1.13 | −1 |
| 7 | T52L | −0.82 | +0.03 | −1 |
| 8 | C62H | −0.38 | −1.26 | −3 |
| 9 | E3Q | −1.36 | −0.41 | +2 |
| 10 | M59N | −0.10 | −2.02 | −2 |

**Ranks 1–2 are meaningfully better supported than 3–10.** D33E is the only candidate clearly positive in both channels (refold: pLDDT 0.885, identical to WT; TM 0.971). R51K is the single best ESM-2 score of all 100 — the model actively prefers K over R there (−0.14 vs −2.05) — and refolds almost exactly onto WT (TM 0.996, RMSD 0.19 Å). Ranks 3–10 are a low-risk-filler tier, not confident positives.

**What would overturn them:** for R51K/R53K, an arginine-specific bidentate contact that lysine can't replace — precisely what sequence models blur. For D33E, a metal or DNA contact where the extra methylene misplaces the carboxylate. For A25Q, actual burial at position 25 (my weakest structural assumption in the top six). C62H sits at rank 8 rather than higher because BLOSUM −3 is a genuine warning I'm partly discounting: if the lone Cys is a metal ligand, it's severe.

## Rejected, with reasoning

~55 variants were penalized by both channels in agreement (I23E/G/C, Y61E, L44S, F32T, L27C, K39C, R42T/M/L, V24S, and similar core/backbone hits).

The interesting rejects are the **channel-disagreement class**: F17A (+0.08), S18F (+0.02), and A49L (+0.53) look neutral-to-good on ESM-2 but draw −7.5 to −15.7 nat penalties from ESM-IF1 — the signature of cavity creation at buried sites. I refolded F17A as a direct test: the fold survives (TM 0.971) but pLDDT drops to 0.864, the largest decrease of any refold I ran. I sided with the structure channel. **A49L is the one I'd promote first** if burial at 49 turns out to be low — an MSA or a working DSSP run would decide it.

The honest caveat: TM-align didn't discriminate anything here. All three refolds scored 0.97–0.996 against WT, so fold retention separated nothing; only pLDDT and ESM-IF1 did the work. And a real MSA could plausibly reorder ranks 3–10 entirely.
